title: An exogenous gradient makes self-assembly more robust for larger ensembles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: An exogenous gradient makes self-assembly more robust for larger ensembles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the active-inference morphogenesis simulations, an exogenous concentration gradient is not necessary but yields a more robust solution for larger ensembles (more than four clones) and fixes the orientation of the target morphology relative to an external frame of reference.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This is not a necessary component of the scheme; however, our simulations suggest that it underwrites a more robust solution for larger ensembles (with more than four clones).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Conclusion”. Scope: Active-inference morphogenesis simulation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-09: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is an explicit comparison between two simulation conditions with standard measurable outputs. The model description and public numerical tools make a direct computational test feasible.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run ensembles of more than four cells with and without the exogenous gradient across seeds, measuring target-form success, convergence time, and orientation. A gradient-dependent increase in success and fixed orientation supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Robustness requires a chosen distribution of initial states and noise levels.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.9
data existence: 0.85
discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ensemble size and an exogenous input are parameters of a public, specified model, so the comparison can be recomputed. The published file does not contain the sweep, and the claim does not fix the robustness measure, so the result is only partly pinned down by what is already runnable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sweep ensemble size above and below four clones in the public model with the exogenous gradient present and removed, and score orientation error and failure rate against a pre-specified robustness statistic. A flat or reversed size effect would refute the reported threshold.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Robustness is not given a numeric definition in the claim.

The current script fixes the exogenous cause at zero and does not ship the size sweep.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.48
data existence: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.62
